title: PowerPoint on Mac: reference SharePoint and OneDrive files when creating a presentation with Copilot Agent Mode
summary: The briefing's feature description and release facts match Microsoft's sources, and both administration paths and PowerShell calls are documented. It appropriately distinguishes general Copilot licensing and SharePoint discovery controls from the unresolved entitlement, default state and handling of explicitly named files.

claims.claim: Roadmap item 555897 concerns referencing SharePoint-library and OneDrive-folder files when creating a presentation with Agent Mode in PowerPoint.
claims.quote: You can now reference files saved in SharePoint libraries and OneDrive folders when creating a presentation with Agent Mode in PowerPoint.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Scope; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Copilot in PowerPoint recognizes SharePoint and OneDrive files mentioned by file or document name in a prompt.
claims.quote: Copilot in PowerPoint can now recognize references to files stored in SharePoint and OneDrive when you mention them in your prompt, such as by file or document name.

claims.claim: Implicit file references were previously unsupported for files in those locations.
claims.quote: Previously, these implicit file references were not supported for files stored in these locations.

claims.claim: The release note instructs users to reference the document name and/or document owner.
claims.quote: In your prompt, reference a file saved in SharePoint or OneDrive by the document name and/or owner of the document.

claims.claim: A user can ask Copilot to create a presentation using the named file as context.
claims.quote: You can naturally reference a relevant file in your prompt, and Copilot can use that file as context when creating your presentation.

claims.claim: Users need not first locate and manually attach or upload the source file.
claims.quote: You can bring existing SharePoint and OneDrive content into your presentation workflow more naturally, without first locating the file and manually attaching it.

claims.claim: The sources do not state the feature-specific default state.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Copilot implicit file references default automatic rollout administrator policy. Opened roadmap 555897 and Learn release notes; the entry specifies user prompt steps but no feature-specific default.

claims.claim: No feature-specific administration setting for implicit PowerPoint file references is documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Copilot reference files SharePoint OneDrive implicit document name 555897 default admin disable setting Graph PowerShell; PowerPoint reference files admin. Opened release notes, Copilot overview and Restricted Content Discovery; no specific switch documented.

claims.claim: The release notes describe gradual deployment to a subset of tenant users before expansion across the organisation.
claims.quote: Copilot features are introduced using a safe deployment model, gradually rolling out to a subset of users within a tenant before expanding across the organization.

claims.claim: The briefing treats this as a review item because the published feature instructions specify no mandatory administrator action or replacement of an existing workflow.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Copilot implicit file references default automatic rollout administrator policy. Opened roadmap 555897 and the complete release-note entry; user presentation steps are given, with no required admin action or replacement of an existing workflow.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Copilot presents only data the individual can already access, so using a file by name does not grant additional permission.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot presents only data that each individual can access using the same underlying controls for data access used in other Microsoft 365 services.

claims.where: controls[0].governs; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery limits selected SharePoint content in organisation-wide search and Microsoft Copilot discovery.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery helps you limit discovery of content from specific SharePoint sites, including recently interacted files, in organization-wide search results and Microsoft Copilot responses while those reviews are taking place.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is a site-level setting.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery is a site-level setting.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery supports SharePoint sites, not OneDrive sites.
claims.quote: You can only apply this feature to SharePoint sites. It's not supported for OneDrive sites.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery changes discoverability rather than existing permissions.
claims.quote: No. Restricted Content Discovery affects discoverability, not access permissions. Users who already have access to content can continue to access it.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions

claims.quote: Searched: Restricted Content Discovery PowerPoint explicitly referenced file prompt name access; Restricted Content Discovery named PowerPoint. Opened RCD and PowerPoint release notes; tenant-wide discovery and open-document exclusions are stated, but this prompt case is not.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery changes for sites with more than 500,000 items can take more than a week to process.
claims.quote: For sites with more than 500,000 items, an update to Restricted Content Discovery could take more than a week to fully process and reflect in search and Copilot experiences.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Indirect cost; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery can be configured when the organisation is licensed for Copilot and has SharePoint Advanced Management available.
claims.quote: You can configure Restricted Content Discovery if your organization is licensed for Copilot and has SharePoint Advanced Management available.

claims.claim: By default, only SharePoint administrators can manage Restricted Content Discovery.
claims.quote: By default, only SharePoint administrators can manage Restricted Content Discovery.

claims.claim: License Administrator or User Administrator is the minimum role for the documented licence-assignment procedure.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is configured at SharePoint admin center > Sites > Active sites > site > Settings > Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote: In the SharePoint admin center, expand Sites and select Active sites. Select the site you want to configure. Open the Settings tab, and then turn Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot on.

claims.claim: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true enables Restricted Content Discovery for the site.
claims.quote:
Enable Restricted Content Discovery for a site
Use PowerShell
Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true

claims.claim: User licence assignment is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses.
claims.quote: In the admin center, go to the Users > Active users page. Select the row of the user that you want to assign a license to. In the right pane, select Licenses and Apps. Expand the Licenses section, select the boxes for the licenses that you want to assign

claims.claim: Microsoft Graph PowerShell assigns a user licence with Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @().
claims.quote:
To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell.
Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: Assigning the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on governs that licence tier rather than all access to Copilot in PowerPoint.
claims.quote: You don't have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license but can use Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote. You have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license with access to the full experience of Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.

claims.claim: The mixed licensing model reflects general Copilot in PowerPoint access through Basic and the add-on tier, not a verified tier for this particular feature.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) refers to users without the Copilot add-on license, but who have access to Copilot capabilities inside apps. Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) is the full add-on licensed experience.
